message.content:
Order filled. Summary:

I reviewed the saved notes (long-term holder, large-cap tech preference, dividends reinvested manually) and the account ($50,000 cash, 100 shares of MSFT, no AAPL position), then checked the AAPL quote at $222.70 last (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72, as of 15:05Z on 2024-11-06). Because the mandate permits AAPL buy orders only up to $10,000 per order and the account had ample cash and no existing AAPL exposure, I bought 40 shares of AAPL with a limit of $223.00 — about $8,920, roughly 0.14% above the last trade and inside the "close to market" constraint and well under both the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap (no other orders today); the order filled at $223.00 for $8,920, leaving the remaining $20,000 daily allowance unused and moving no money out of the account. The decision rested on the fundamentals I looked up from AAPL's FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-11-01): revenue of $391,035 million, net income of $93,736 million, and diluted EPS of $6.08, which are consistent with the large-cap technology profile in the mandate.
